headings.title: SMTO-FIL-0049 — SMTO couldn't check everything in the folder before changing it

html:
SMTO-FIL-0049 — SMTO couldn't check everything in the folder before changing it

GUID: 08303c15-12b1-41ca-9fab-7ef1279dada0
Slug: file-preflight-incomplete
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • Before copying, moving or deleting a whole folder, SMTO looks at everything inside it. It couldn't finish looking, so it didn't start the change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation why its check of the folder didn't finish, for example a folder it wasn't allowed to open, a shortcut that loops back on itself, or too many files. The reason tells you whether to fix access, work on less at once, or remove the looping shortcut.
  2. If a subfolder couldn't be opened, make sure the account SMTO uses on that computer can open it, or ask SMTO to leave that subfolder out. SMTO won't change a folder it couldn't fully see, so every part must be readable.
  3. If the folder is very large or another program keeps changing it, ask SMTO to work on smaller parts one at a time. Smaller parts can be fully checked within SMTO's time and size limits.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the copy, move or delete and tells you how many items it handled.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't move or delete the folder by hand to get around the check while the Task is still running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The recursive preflight for a copy, move or delete stopped because the Walker reported an incomplete traversal (for example permission_denied, symlink_cycle, entry_limit or revision_conflict); no change was started.

What this means

  • Recursive mutation preflight sees a walker reason indicating that the tree inspection could not complete. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Recursive mutation preflight sees a walker reason indicating that the tree inspection could not complete.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect traversal diagnostics for inaccessible or unsupported entries and incomplete bounds.

How to fix it

  • The error_kind is the Walker's first incomplete reason (for example permission_denied, symlink_cycle, entry_limit or revision_conflict); the failing path is not included, and a dry_run repeats the same preflight, so list the tree on the Gateway (a deeper file listing or find) to locate it. Fix access, break the link cycle, raise max_entries_scanned (default 100,000) or narrow the root, then obtain a complete fresh preflight before repeating the operation.
  • Inspect the preflight diagnostics and correct inaccessible or unsupported entries. Obtain a complete fresh preflight before repeating the mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A complete fresh tree preflight covers the intended mutation scope.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
